title: Constructible cohomological interval descent on a finite open cover
statement:
Fix the finite purity coefficients [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme and $X=\bigcup_{t\in J}U_t$ a finite open covering [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with inclusions $u_t:U_t\hookrightarrow X$. The empty family $J=\varnothing$ is allowed when $X=\varnothing$. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and derived open restriction $Lu_t^*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $F\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be arbitrary, with no prior boundedness or etale-origin assumption. Then for any integers $r\leq s$: if $Lu_t^*F\in D_c^{[r,s]}(U_t,A)$ for every $t\in J$, then $F\in D_c^{[r,s]}(X,A)$ [def-weil-constructible-intervals]. No Tor hypothesis is imposed. In particular, if each restriction $Lu_t^*F$ is bounded constructible with its own finite cohomological interval, then $F$ is bounded constructible [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].

For $X=\varnothing$ one has $F=0$, so the implication holds for every displayed interval.
